claim: Every folder a harness session starts in carries the tier hook; before a session is started in a folder, check that the hook is present there and install it if it is not.
when: before starting a session in any folder
quote: If this hook will not work in another folder, then that folder should have another hook of its own. And before starting, we should check if this hook is present there or not.

claim: tools/ensure-tier-hook.sh <folder> says whether the tier hook is wired in that folder and installs it when the folder is inside this repository and has no settings file; it will not install into a folder outside this repository without --force, because other sessions there (the product's) follow other routes and would have their helpers refused.

Two orchestrator sessions on Opus are collecting the literature on bottlenecks (o1: detecting the bottleneck and switching method; o2: scheduling under several scarce resources), and one helper reads our own logs for which resource limited which past job. Reports go to docs/program/evidence/bottleneck-2026-11-18/, records to library/journal/<date>/o1.jsonl and o2.jsonl. The top session commits their files, decides proposed corrections and writes the table from bottleneck to method.

Over 25 recorded episodes of our own work the limit changed from job to job: the serial queue in 8, blocked program starts in 6, memory in 4, the token allowance in 4, the processor in 3 (the model run with 16 workers: 88 to 91 % on average, peaking at 100 %), nothing in 1; five episodes had two limits at once. The processor share of a single job, the memory peak of a model run and the tokens of any run were never measured.
